title: Measure a tyre's tread depth with a pen gauge: probe on a groove's floor, foot flat across the ribs, then lift it off
instruction: Measure the tread depth of the tyre with the tread-depth gauge, then put the gauge back on its rest.
context: Automotive service technicians and mechanics (about 826,000 US workers) and tyre changers measure tread depth on every multipoint inspection, tyre rotation and seasonal tyre swap, with a pen gauge read in 32nds of an inch; here on a wheel with a new tyre, lying flat on the bench. The reading is right only if two contacts are made at once: the probe's tip on the floor of a main groove, not on a rib or on one of the molded wear bars that cross the groove (on a bar it reads 2/32 shallow), while the gauge's T-foot lies flat across the ribs on both sides of the groove, square to the tread (tipped 6 degrees, it reads about 2/32 deep). The gauge's stem is held only by friction, so the gauge must then come straight off without the probe catching the groove's wall. The robot doesn't read the scale: the stem's position is the result, checked by whoever writes up the inspection.
setup: A bench in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Positions in metres from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the left (+) or right (-); heights above the bench. (1) A wheel lying flat (fixed): a new, unused Michelin Defender2 205/55R16 91H tyre (630 mm across, 213 mm tall lying flat, black rubber) mounted on a 16 x 6.5 in steel wheel, about 19 kg, its axis at (0.555, -0.305), straight in front of the right arm; the tread nearest the robot at x 0.240. The tread band runs 21.5 to 191.5 mm up (the tyre's 6.7 in tread width): five ribs and four circumferential grooves, 8, 10, 10 and 8 mm wide, their centres 57.5, 90.5, 122.5 and 155.5 mm up, each 8.33 mm (10.5/32 in, the tyre's published new tread depth) deep. Wear bars 1.59 mm (2/32 in) tall and 8 mm long cross every groove at six places, 60 degrees apart, one of them on the line from the wheel's axis toward the robot. Groove depths, before the first trial: with a digital caliper's depth rod (the end of its beam laid across both ribs), measure each groove at three places within 30 mm of the wear bar facing the robot (not on the bar) and record each groove's mean; use the tyre only if every groove is within 1/32 in of 10.5/32 in (7.5 to 9.1 mm). (2) Milton S-448 tread-depth gauge (aluminium and steel, 27 g, 89 mm long): a barrel 10 mm across and 49 mm long, a T-foot 32 x 8 x 1.5 mm at its front end, and a stem sliding through both: a probe with a 2.8 mm flat tip out of the foot's face and a 6 mm indicator bar out of the barrel's back, graduated 0 to 1 in in 1/32 in. The stem stays where it is put (about 2 N of friction). It starts pushed fully out (probe 25.4 mm past the foot). (3) Its rest (fixed, wood): a board 120 x 60 x 20 mm with a block under the barrel's back end; the gauge lies on it level, axis 36 mm up, pointing forward (+x), foot upright, the foot's face at (0.165, -0.215).
scoring: The reading is how far the probe's tip stands past the foot's face, read on the gauge's scale where the indicator bar leaves the barrel. Seated means the foot flat on the tread (both its ends within 1 mm of the tread surface) with the probe's tip on a groove's floor (within 0.8 mm). 1.0: the gauge was seated at some time, its reading is within 1/32 in (0.8 mm) of the 10.5/32 in (8.33 mm) depth, and it lies back on its rest (foot within 12 mm of its place, level within 5 degrees, pointing forward within 10 degrees, foot upright within 15 degrees), let go (grippers' centre points at least 3 cm from it) and still for 1 s. 0.5: seated, reading within 1/32 in, the gauge off the tyre but not back on its rest (held or not). 0 otherwise: never seated (for example the probe on a rib or a wear bar), or the reading off by more than 1/32 in (foot tipped, or the stem moved while taking it off). Real trial: watch the video for the seated foot, then read the scale and compare it with that groove's depth measured at setup.
reset_notes: Push the gauge's stem fully out (probe 1 in past the foot) and lay the gauge on its rest, foot upright, pointing at the wheel. The wheel stays where it is. Nothing is used up.
fidelity: Rigid bodies (PhysX). The tyre is rigid and fixed (no rubber give under the few-newton press); its tread is flat 1.5 degree segments, flat across its width, straight-walled grooves, no sipes. Estimates: the stem's 2 N friction, the foot, barrel and blade sizes (scaled from the maker's photo against its 3.5 in length), the groove and rib widths and the bars' 8 mm length. The stem also has light damping (solver stabiliser). The pocket clip and the printed scale are not modelled.
